correctness.rationale: Exact exhaustive twenty-permutation cell enumeration returns counts (5,20,60,80,20). All signed integer boundary compositions vanish and their nonzero Smith factors are 4,16,43,20 copies of 1, giving precisely free reduced integral homology Z in degree 2 and Z^17 in degree 3. Each top 4-cell possesses a different free 3-face, allowing twenty explicit elementary collapses. The 2-skeleton agrees with that of the simply connected full injective-word complex on five letters. In the resulting three-dimensional complex, unimodular row/column changes on the 43 primitive attaching classes yield a homotopy wedge S^2 and seventeen S^3. An explicit integral closed 2-cochain is not a coboundary, and its translation and multiplier transformations give the H2 character. Signed fixed-word Lefschetz traces on all 20 elements give the rational H3 character. The embedded checker verifies every finite computation; none is extrapolated to an infinite family.

originality.rationale: Statement-wise comparison of the full primary papers with actual searches did not find an affine-five-letter subgroup classification or its 17-dimensional rational symmetry module. Govc proves free fundamental group only, and Chachólski–Levi–Meshulam study the full injective-word complex and arbitrary two-permutation realizations. The natural twenty-permutation group and its action are not consequences of those results. An indexed Paley-seventeen flag-complex calculation concerns a different affine action on a different object. Unindexed or non-OA subgroup computations remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The affine group AGL(1,5) is the canonical smallest proper sharply 2-transitive five-point group, so its ordered-word topology is an intrinsic and motivated case of permutation complexes, not an arbitrary engineered example. It exhibits simultaneous degree-two and degree-three integral homology whereas the full injective-word complex has homology only in degree four. The nontrivial quadratic character in rank-one second homology and the explicit 17-dimensional third rational representation provide finer geometric information relevant for symmetry-sensitive topology beyond Betti ranks. No unproved extension to other primes is needed to motivate this exact classification.
